note: The hand-kept part of the Machines catalogue (schema/MACHINE_CATALOGUE.md): what each kind of machine is and does, which group it stands in, which species' records name it, and where its size, count and proteins are read. tools/build_catalogue.py reads this file, the species files, the species' own proteins and the machine files, and writes data/catalogue/catalogue.json. No number is written here that a source does not give, and no sentence of a paper but the one quoted with its place. The membrane units of the law inventory are not listed here: the page reads them from the scene's protein units, as the Protein atlas does.
decided: The tab and its catalogue were asked for on 17 November 2026: a catalogue of molecular machines by species, gathered as the proteins were, in a design of its own. Decided 17 November 2026 (D209): the tab is the first milestone (M0) of the engine's path for machines, a catalogue with drawing levels labelled illustration; no machine is in the engine, and the drawing levels are the viewer's, not simulation detail. The coordinator ruled the same evening that a machine keeps one identity on the page.

groups.label: Making proteins
groups.plain: Machines that read a messenger RNA and build the protein it codes for.

groups.label: Reading genes
groups.plain: Machines that copy a gene's DNA into RNA.

groups.label: Copying and mending DNA
groups.plain: Machines that copy a cell's DNA before it divides, hold its strands and mend them.

groups.label: Making ATP
groups.plain: Machines that make the cell's fuel from a flow of ions across a membrane.

groups.label: Capturing light
groups.plain: Machines of the chloroplast that catch light, make ATP and NADPH from it, and fix carbon dioxide.

groups.label: Moving ions: units of the law inventory
groups.plain: Channels, pumps, exchangers and junctions: the units of the engine's law inventory that are protein assemblies, as the Protein atlas lists them. A unit's panel says which of its laws an active model declares.

groups.label: Putting proteins into membranes
groups.plain: Channels that thread new proteins across a membrane or set them into it.

groups.label: Folding proteins
groups.plain: Cages and rings that give a new protein a closed space to fold in, using ATP.

groups.label: Breaking proteins down
groups.plain: Proteases that unfold proteins and cut them, using ATP.

groups.label: Moving, sensing and attaching
groups.plain: Machines that move the cell, steer it, or hold it to a surface.

groups.label: Cell surface
groups.plain: Structures that coat the cell or extend from its surface.

groups.label: Metabolism
groups.plain: Enzymes and their assemblies that transform small molecules.

groups.label: Binding and stress response
groups.plain: Proteins that bind ions or sugars, or are associated with a stress response.

groups.label: Electron transfer
groups.plain: Proteins that pass electrons between molecules.

groups.label: Carrying cargo
groups.plain: Motors that walk along the cell's filaments, carrying cargo from place to place.

groups.label: Particles whose job is not known
groups.plain: Large particles whose function has not been found.
groups.stands_why: Decided 19 November 2026: this group's tray stands at the back of the bench, behind the tray of the law inventory's units. Its one particle, the vault, is the largest shape on a bench; in the row before that tray it stood in front of the units' small shapes at the opening view and hid them.

groups.label: Organelles
groups.plain: The cell's own compartments, each far larger than any machine: they stand on a shelf behind the bench, at the bench's one scale.
groups.stands_why: Asked for on 20 November 2026: the organelles stand in the Machines view as the machines do, on a shelf above the bench, drawn with the Cell view's own models at the bench's one scale, and travelled to. They are no machines: in no tray and no count of machines.

units.unit.U47: a passive permeability of the mitochondrial inner membrane

kinds.label: Ribosome
kinds.plain: Reads a messenger RNA and joins amino acids, one at a time, into the protein it codes for.

kinds.label: RNA polymerase
kinds.plain: Copies a gene's DNA into RNA, the first step from a gene to a protein.

kinds.label: ATP synthase
kinds.plain: Turns as ions flow through it across a membrane, and makes ATP as it turns; run the other way, it spends ATP to pump ions out.

records.says: Decided 17 November 2026 (D209): the ATP synthase is to be the first machine built in the engine (M1), as general pieces, after the core-seams pass; its law is to be D193's proton_coupled_atp_synthesis_cycle@1, built by the mitochondria lane. There is no model of it yet.

kinds.label: Protein translocon
kinds.plain: A channel in the membrane that threads a new protein across it, or opens sideways to set it into the membrane.

kinds.label: FtsH protease
kinds.plain: A protease that stands in the cell membrane and unfolds and cuts proteins, using ATP.

kinds.label: Lon protease
kinds.plain: A protease that unfolds and cuts proteins inside the cell, using ATP.

kinds.label: HslUV protease
kinds.plain: A barrel of HslV that cuts proteins, capped by a ring of HslU that unfolds them and feeds them in, using ATP. HslV's subunits carry the signature of the proteasome's.

kinds.label: Chemoreceptor array
kinds.plain: A lattice of receptor proteins in the membrane that senses chemicals and steers the cell's swimming toward food.

kinds.label: Attachment organelle
kinds.plain: A membrane protrusion at one pole with an internal core: it carries the adhesins that hold the cell to a surface, and leads the cell when it glides.

kinds.label: Nucleus
kinds.plain: Holds the cell's DNA inside a double membrane, the nuclear envelope, whose pores let molecules in and out; the nucleolus inside it is where ribosomes are put together.

kinds.label: Endoplasmic reticulum
kinds.plain: A network of membrane sheets and tubes that runs on from the nuclear envelope: the rough sheets, studded with ribosomes, make proteins for membranes and for export, and the network stores calcium.

kinds.label: Golgi apparatus
kinds.plain: Stacks of flattened sacs, the cisternae, where proteins made at the endoplasmic reticulum are modified, sorted and sent on in vesicles.

kinds.label: Mitochondrion
kinds.plain: An organelle of two membranes, the inner one folded into cristae, where most of a cell's ATP is made.

kinds.label: Chloroplast
kinds.plain: A plant cell's organelle of light: two envelope membranes round stacks of membrane discs, where photosynthesis captures light and fixes carbon dioxide.

kinds.label: Vacuole
kinds.plain: A plant cell's large sac of water and solutes, bounded by one membrane: it fills most of the cell and holds it taut against its wall.

kinds.label: Lysosome
kinds.plain: A sac of digestive enzymes in an acid lumen, bounded by one membrane, where the cell breaks down what it takes in and its own worn parts.

kinds.label: COPI vesicle
kinds.plain: A small vesicle coated with coatomer (COPI) that carries cargo between the Golgi's cisternae and back to the endoplasmic reticulum.

kinds.label: Peroxisome
kinds.plain: A small organelle of one membrane where fatty acids are broken down and hydrogen peroxide is made and destroyed.

kinds.label: Lipid droplet
kinds.plain: A store of fat in the cytoplasm: neutral lipids wrapped in a single layer of phospholipids, from which the cell draws fatty acids and sterols.

kinds.label: Autophagosome
kinds.plain: A sphere of two membranes that closes round worn parts of the cell and other cargo and carries them to a lysosome, where they are broken down (autophagy).

kinds.label: Centriole
kinds.plain: A short barrel of nine triplets of microtubules. Two of them at right angles, in a cloud of protein, make the centrosome, which organises the cell's microtubules.

kinds.label: Endocytic vesicle
kinds.plain: A small vesicle or short tubule of membrane taken in from the cell's surface and marked by the protein Rab5: among the first stations of the way in (endocytosis), before the early endosome.

measures.note: Sizes measured by the viewer from a Protein Data Bank entry's coordinates with tools/measure_particle.py: the tool's own output, kept here as written. A species' file that states a part's size of its own (cell.parts.ribosome) is read first, and the measure here is then not used. The Protein Data Bank states no size: each number is the viewer's own.

membrane.says: Where its membrane lies: the entry holds no membrane, so a thin slab stands where the ring stands, an illustration, centred on the ring and as thick as the ring's farthest atoms reach along the machine's axis

ecoli-rna-polymerase.note: the σ70 holoenzyme, with no DNA
ecoli-rna-polymerase.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: kept over the core enzyme 7MKP (3.41 Å), which the gathering ranked first: the σ70 holoenzyme holds the machine more whole for a visitor.

ecoli-translocon.note: SecYEG alone, measured from an entry where it holds YidC and sits on a ribosome, both left out; only about half of SecG's sequence stands in its coordinates

ecoli-hslv.note: HslV's barrel of twelve capped by one HslU ring of six, the crystal's biological assembly; capped at both ends beside it
ecoli-hslv.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: kept over 1HT1 (2.8 Å, the barrel capped at both ends), which the gathering ranked first. With a cap at each end the frame from the barrel to a cap is degenerate, as 1G4B's is (the caps' centre sits on the barrel's), so the parts would not stand upright by this measure until the two caps are named by chain; the doubly capped machine stands beside it as a whole.

human-proteasome.note: the 26S proteasome with one regulatory particle; the entry's title names ZFAND5, of which it holds no chain; it holds 32 of the 54 proteins its dossier names with the proteasome
human-proteasome.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call, its parts grouped as the Gene Ontology's terms on its dossier's rows group them: the core particle (proteasome core complex, GO:0005839), the regulatory particle's base (GO:0008540) and its lid (GO:0008541); the frame from the core to the lid.

core.label: Core particle (20S): the α and β rings

base.label: Regulatory particle's base: its six ATPases, Rpn1, Rpn2 and Rpn10

membrane.says: Where its membrane lies: the entry holds no membrane, so a thin slab stands where the ring stands, an illustration, centred on the ring and as thick as the ring's farthest atoms reach along the machine's axis

human-atp-synthase.note: the mitochondrial ATP synthase, one monomer; it holds 16 of the 21 proteins its dossier names with it
human-atp-synthase.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call, its parts grouped as UniProt names the subunits on its dossier's rows: F(1) α and β the head; F(1) γ, δ and ε the central stalk; the peripheral stalk's b, d, F6 and OSCP; F(0) c the ring; F(0) a, 8, e, f, g and j the stator's foot, as E. coli's are drawn; the frame from the ring to the head.

stator-foot.label: Stator's foot in the membrane (a, A6L, e, f, g, j)

human-rna-polymerase.note: RNA polymerase II with Gdown1 (POLR2M), one of the proteins its dossier names with it
human-rna-polymerase.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call. No part is named: its dossier's rows give no sub-assembly of it, so it is drawn as its whole, then each chain.

human-rna-polymerase-i.note: RNA polymerase I with RRN3 bound, which is left out of the measure
human-rna-polymerase-i.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call. No part is named: its dossier's rows give no sub-assembly of it, so it is drawn as its whole, then each chain.

human-complex-i.note: in the frame from subunit ND1 to NDUFV1 its matrix arm stands upright, and its membrane arm slopes about 20° below level
human-complex-i.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call, with a frame from MT-ND1 to NDUFV1 added. Its two arms are not named yet: its dossier's rows give no sub-assembly of it, and no rule from the measure is settled, so it is drawn as its whole, then each chain.

human-mitochondrial-ribosome.note: translating: its mRNA, its tRNAs (the structural tRNAVal among them) and the nascent chain are left out of the measure
human-mitochondrial-ribosome.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call: its two subunits as the Gene Ontology's terms on its dossier's rows group them (the mitochondrial large and small ribosomal subunits, GO:0005762 and GO:0005763); the frame from the large subunit to the small one.

human-cmg-helicase.note: bound to DNA, which is left out of the measure
human-cmg-helicase.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: the gathering's pick, by the stated ranking of its dossier's rules.structure, measured with its dossier's call, its parts grouped as UniProt names the proteins on its dossier's rows: the six MCM licensing factors, the four GINS proteins, and Cdc45; no frame named: the tool's own axes.

animals-ribosome.note: the whole 80S, with the antibiotic tigecycline bound, which is no polymer and is not measured; RACK1 (entity 70), whose name says neither subunit, stands in the small subunit, where the measure's call places it
animals-ribosome.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: of three entries of the whole human 80S measured with the tool, 8YOP (2.2 Å) is the best resolved and holds both subunits whole with no tRNA or factor bound. 6QZP (2.9 Å, an E-site tRNA bound) and 4V6X (5.0 Å, ranked first by the gathering for holding the most of the human's ribosome proteins: 79 entities named as ribosome proteins, against 8YOP's 77 and 6QZP's 75, by the names in each entry) give the same whole within 2 nm (29.4 to 29.7 by 23.0 to 23.2 by 20.8 to 22.8 nm). 6QZP's share of each sequence in its coordinates reads 98 to 100% because its deposited sequences hold little more than its modelled residues (its uL4 is 368 residues long; 8YOP's and 4V6X's, 427).

animals-serca.chosen: Decided 17 November 2026: 6LLE, the human SERCA2b, is the unit's own protein (UniProt P16615, SERCA2); the Protein atlas names rabbit SERCA1a, 1SU4, among the unit's reference structures.

animals-ip3r.note: the type 3 receptor, a tetramer, with no ligand bound

animals-kv1-2.note: Kv1.2 with four β2 subunits, the crystal's biological assembly; by its own records, a re-refinement of the diffraction data of entry 2A79

animals-connexin-channel.note: connexin 43, two docked connexons of six, in a nanodisc

parts.connexon-1: A connexon, in one cell's membrane
parts.connexon-2: A connexon, in the other cell's membrane

human-vault.note: the vault cage with ADP, the first biological assembly of 78 copies of the major vault protein; the entry holds no PARP4, TEP1 or vault RNA
human-vault.chosen: Decided 19 November 2026: the best entry by resolution among the human entries that hold the whole particle and whose assembly file is held (the gathering's rule for the vault: its first assembly holds 78 copies of a major vault protein entity covering at least 70 per cent of the protein); two entries of a better resolution are not held. Its two parts are its half-vaults, told apart by the side of the plane across the long axis (the measure's x = 0) on which a chain's centre lies: 39 chains each.

half-a.label: A half-vault: 39 chains, on the positive side of the long axis

half-b.label: The other half-vault: 39 chains, on the negative side

unit_sizes.note: Decided 17 November 2026 (step C of the Machines tab): a unit of the law inventory takes a size only from a structure of its own kind, of any organism, and its panel names that organism; where a species' atlas finds the unit built from another family, from a structure of that family. A unit with no such structure stays a card. These sizes stand on the animals' benches; the units of the other species stay cards.
